reason: The sources provide rich, cross-verified details from multiple space agency and observatory releases supporting a compelling 45-second narrative.
story: On October 9, 2022, space telescopes detected an explosion so intense it temporarily blinded their detectors. Cataloged as GRB 221009A, astronomers quickly named it the BOAT—the Brightest Of All Time. Originating around two billion light-years away in the constellation Sagitta, the blast was triggered by a dying massive star collapsing into a black hole. It launched narrow jets of particles near the speed of light pointed directly at Earth, making it up to 70 times brighter than any gamma-ray burst ever recorded. The explosion's radiation traveled for billions of years across deep space, physically ionized Earth's upper atmosphere, and disrupted longwave radio communications. X-rays from the blast also scattered off interstellar dust, producing brilliant concentric rings. Astronomers estimate a cosmic explosion this intense only strikes Earth once every 10,000 years.
angle: A cosmic explosion two billion light-years away was so intense it blinded space telescopes and physically warped Earth's upper atmosphere.

claims.claim: GRB 221009A was detected by orbiting space telescopes on October 9, 2022.
The explosion originated in the direction of the constellation Sagitta.
Astronomers nicknamed the event the BOAT, short for Brightest Of All Time.
The event was triggered by the collapse of a massive star creating a black hole.
The explosion occurred roughly 1.9 to 2.4 billion light-years away from Earth.
GRB 221009A was up to 70 times brighter than the previous record-holding gamma-ray burst.
The radiation was so intensely bright that it blinded and saturated gamma-ray detectors on space telescopes.
Scientists estimated a gamma-ray burst this energetic is a once-in-10,000-year event to hit Earth.
The exploding star launched narrow jets of material moving near the speed of light directed right at Earth.
The burst emitted radiation photons carrying energies in the tera-electron volt (TeV) range.
Radiation from the burst physically altered and ionized Earth's upper atmosphere (ionosphere).
The atmospheric disturbance disrupted longwave radio communications on Earth.
X-ray radiation scattering off galactic dust created concentric rings around the burst's position.
The burst was observed by NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory.

disputed: Distance measurement: S1 and S4 report 2.4 billion light-years, while S3 and S6 state 1.9 billion light-years. Script should generalize to 'about two billion light-years away'.

Supernova detection: S1 states JWST confirmed a Type Ic supernova, whereas S6 states searches with JWST had not yet conclusively found a supernova. Script should focus on the collapse into a black hole.
